newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Spector opens firmer after suspension.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Spector opens firmer after suspension.

text.p: Shares in Belgian photo-processor Spector opened at 2,000 francs on Monday, up 70 francs from 1,930 at the close on Wednesday when the stock was suspended on the Brussels bourse.
The company announced on Friday it planned to raise its share capital by about two billion Belgian francs in order to finance the purchase of Swiss Porst's activities and Interdiscount France.

The capital increase will be conducted through the issue of preferential subscription rights to existing shareholders. Porst Holding has said it will use its preferential rights to subscribe to 50.2 percent of the capital increase.
In addition, Spector intends to issue subordinated, convertible bonds with a warrant for an amount between 1.0 billion and 1.5 billion Belgian francs.
"I'm positive on the share. One of the main problems was going to be how the acquisitions would be financed," one analyst said, adding that the company had put in place "an intelligent scheme".
Several analysts said they took a positive view on Spector's stock, though they noted that not all details of the operation would be known until the prospectus was published.
"There's still a lot of paper coming into the market, though these share price levels seem acceptable," one said, adding that the shares were likely to continue rising in the medium term.
